Subject: Staged switchover validation: canary telemetry shim + questions

Hi Sara / Stratus ops,

Thanks for the RFP addendum — attached is a concise canary runbook and a short questionnaire we use for validation during pilot -> canary -> full cutover. TL;DR: our recommended staged ramp is 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% over a minimum 72-hour window, with clear rollback triggers tied to error rate, latency, and model quality regressions.

What were asking you to confirm in your replies:
- Preferred cutover calendar (weekdays vs weekend) and blackout windows
- Telemetry endpoints you want us to push traces/metrics to (Datadog/Prometheus/None)
- Encryption and egress constraints for logs/metrics
- Any minimum throughput or peak-sustained qps expectations during canary

Attachments: redwood-canary-runbook-v1.pdf (runbook + rollback criteria)

Key notes in the runbook:
- Preflight: traffic-splitting stubbed at reverse-proxy layer; canary instances run pinned to model v1.3-quant.
- Telemetry shim: prefix-based KV cache metrics + per-token latency histograms exported via OTLP.
- Fallback: automatic route diversion to warm fallback pool if 5-min error rate > 2.5% or p95 latency increases > 1000ms.

Ava / Priyom — copying you to confirm the technical bits below are feasible for Stratus on-prem networking and for the Dedicated offering if they choose reserved capacity.

Sara — once you confirm the items above well update the runbook and circulate a final validated schedule and kickoff invite.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0129

Markus, thanks for the quick deck and runbook — this looks like a good starting point. A few clarifying questions from our ops team: 

1) Telemetry/PII: You reference OTLP exports and token-level histograms. Can you confirm: are any user prompt texts or embeddings exported in clear text? We need assurance that PII is never transmitted to external telemetry endpoints.

2) Traffic split control: Our reverse proxy team prefers to own the traffic-split at the edge. Do you require feature flags or will a simple header-based routing gate suffice?

3) Ramp cadence: your 1/5/20/100% looks standard — can you provide an alternate condensed weekend plan (24-48h) in case stakeholders push for a condensed timeline?

4) Fallback pools: what are expected cold-start times for fallback pools and are those pools using different quantization profiles (tradeoff: cost vs latency)?

Wed like to confirm answers before we share this with our security/compliance reviewer. Also please send a connectivity diagram (ports/IPs) we can give to our network team.

Regards,
Sara Lindstrom
Head, Cloud Ops | Stratus Bank
+1 (212) 555-7891

Subject: Re: Staged switchover validation: canary telemetry shim + questions

Sara — good questions, answered inline below. I also attached a connectivity matrix and a small set of terraform snippets for the networking / routing bits.

1) Telemetry/PII: We never export raw prompt text or embeddings to external telemetry by default. The telemetry shim emits aggregate counters and histograms (per-route token counts, p50/p95/p99 latency buckets, cache hit ratio) and an anonymized model-quality delta metric (hash-based prompt set fingerprinting, not raw prompts). If you require telemetry to remain on-prem only, we can switch to OTLP over TLS to your collector inside the VPC with no external egress.

2) Traffic split control: Header-based routing is sufficient — we add a X-Canary-Version header and accept either edge-level split or our sidecar flag. For your setup the simplest is edge-controlled split (reverse proxy owns percentages) and we observe via telemetry.

3) Condensed weekend plan (24-48h): recommended compressed cadence: 5% (4h) -> 25% (12h) -> 75% (24h) -> 100% (remaining 8-12h), but only if ops can approve near-real-time telemetry refresh (1m scrape) and a 2-person on-call for the 48h window. We will not recommend compressed cadence if your model-quality evals are manual or have >2h lag.

4) Fallback pool cold-start: warm fallback pool (pre-warmed by container pool) typical cold-start < 30s; if fallback uses a cheaper quantized variant cold-starts are similar since image is warm, but p95 latency may increase by 150-300ms depending on q-profile. We recommend keeping at least 2 warm fallback nodes per availability zone for production canaries.

Attachments included: connectivity-matrix-stratus.xlsx, tf-snippets-redwood-onprem.tf

Ava / Priyom: can you confirm the on-prem OTLP path and the ability to pin fallback pools to different quant profiles? Also note: if they choose a Dedicated reserved capacity we can pre-provision warm fallback nodes to shorten cold-start risk.

Thanks,
Markus

Quick confirmation from runtime: we support OTLP over TLS to a customer-hosted collector (no external egress by default). Model pinning and quant profiles are fully supported per lane; note that KV cache behavior differs across quant profiles — smaller quantization may reduce cache hit ratio slightly due to tokenization nuances.

Operational caveat: if Stratus wants sub-1s p95 at 100% traffic you should plan on Dedicated reserved capacity (we can quote separately). For canary and condensed weekend plan the 1m scrape cadence is fine as Markus suggested — but our platform emits per-token histograms which can increase cardinality; recommend sampling at the route-level (not per-user) for telemetry retention reasons.

Ava
Senior PM, Runtime | Redwood Inference

Sara / Markus — operational playbook notes below plus a short preflight checklist (attached). Ive also shared a hole-punched Drive link for the runbook.

Preflight (72h before pilot):
- Confirm firewall rules: outbound OTLP port 4317 to collector IPs 
- Verify TLS client certs (we can provide CSR template)
- Run synthetic load on the staging route to validate p95 and cache-hit behavior
- Confirm rollback contact list and PagerDuty escalation group

Canary automation steps:
1) Day 0: Deploy canary instances pinned to model v1.3-quant, warm up caches with synthetic warmers
2) Traffic split: edge-controlled header with X-Canary-Version -> observe for 30m at 1%
3) If stable, escalate to 5% for 2h, then 20% for 6h, then 100% over remaining window (standard plan).
4) Automated gating: if any gating rule trips (error rate, model quality delta, latency p95), execute immediate rollback and route all traffic to fallback pool.

Rollback matrix:
- Error spike > 2.5% sustained 5-min -> immediate rollback
- Model-quality delta > threshold on black-box eval -> manual hold + 30-min hold window
- Networking anomaly -> divert to warm fallback and open incident

Attachments: preflight-checklist.md
Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-canary-runbook

Priyom Das
Sr. SRE, Orchestration | Redwood Inference
